categories.name: Accuracy
categories.reason: Season counts and 2026 averages come from FCB season files. Shares are ppg and mpg times games. Mitchell's row is 1,085.9 against 1,086 on the WNBA.com awards story. Collier's one-year deal, the cap, the dates, and the core rule are quoted from the Lynx game notes or the WNBPA CBA PDF. Contract length is left blank where no team document states it. The league's official service ledger is not in the file, and the page says so.

categories.name: Information gain
categories.reason: Every 2026 regular-season player is classified by the CBA years-of-service test, and each team's share of points and minutes is split across that test. CBS has a top 10. Her Hoop Stats has names. Neither publishes this production split or the season-count check on Kuier, Engstler, and Burrell.

categories.name: Effort and replication cost
categories.reason: 2008-2026 season files, the CBA PDF, team notes, and the league lottery and awards pages, plus a ranked chart, two CSVs, and a data dictionary. Not a hand log of every box score.

categories.name: Originality
categories.reason: The angle is the service-class share of 2026 scoring, with Las Vegas at 96.3% and the league at 56.0%, and an explicit line that this is not yet the February free-agent list.

categories.name: Experience and expertise
categories.reason: Real byline linked to the author page. No interview. Primary documents are linked in the body.

categories.name: Main content and layout
categories.reason: Finding is the H1 and the one-line lead. The team table sits under the lead photo. The player table, dates, and disagreements follow. Fine print is last. Title tag is a shorter form of the same finding.

categories.name: Transparency
categories.reason: Standard how-this-story-was-made note, CC0 downloads, data dictionary, photo credit, and the gaps (unsigned contract lengths, short seasons, two unsplit rows, no February list) are on the page.

categories.name: Writing craft
categories.reason: Sentence-case headline, plain sentences, no em dashes. In-article links open in a new tab. A few player notes still open on the stat line.

categories.name: People-first purpose
categories.reason: A reader who wants the 2027 class gets the CBA dates, the status rule, every 2026 player's class, and which public labels the season count can and cannot settle.

categories.name: Human voice
categories.reason: Specific and cautious. The disagreement section still repeats a stat-line rhythm. No stock AI phrases.

unique: Las Vegas got 96.3% of its 2026 points, and 96.0% of its minutes, from players with five or more seasons. League-wide that group scored 56.0% of points and played 54.1% of minutes.
The player file is the CBA test (Article VI, Sections 5, 8, and 9), not a copy of a published free-agent list. Qualifying offers still decide restricted and reserved status.
Core eligibility for 2027 is the six-year line in Article VI, Section 7(b). Exhibit 4 does not say which 2027 core spots are already filled.
